title: Watchers flew to Mount Hermon in advanced aerospace craft

tellings.quote: I think that's how the watchers got to the summit of Mount Hermon by the way at the helms at the helms of of of advanced aerospace vehicles what we would describe today as UFOs.
So when the Watchers descended to Mount Hermon, I believe that they were at the helms of advanced aerospace vehicles.
tellings.link_reason: Both tell the same theory: the Watchers reached Mount Hermon piloting advanced aerospace vehicles.

as_told.title: Watchers descend to Mount Hermon in aerospace vehicles

tellings.quote: And they were in all two hundred; who descended ⌜in the days⌝ of =Jared= on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.
But you were ⌜formerly⌝ spiritual, living the eternal life, and immortal for all generations of the world.
And therefore I have not appointed wives for you; for as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling.

plain: The idea is that the Watchers, the fallen angels of the Book of Enoch, an ancient Jewish text that most Bibles leave out, did not simply float down from heaven but flew to Mount Hermon at the controls of advanced craft, what we would now call UFOs. A guest named Tim Alberino, who reads the old texts this way, says it twice on the same episode, each time as his own belief: 'I believe that they were at the helms of advanced aerospace vehicles.' The book itself, in R. H. Charles's 1917 translation, says the two hundred 'descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon,' where they swore an oath together. Later in the book God tells the Watchers they were 'formerly spiritual, living the eternal life, and immortal,' and that 'as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling.' So the text tells of spirits coming down from heaven to a mountaintop, in that order. Turning that descent into a landing by pilots in machines is Alberino's reading, which the book neither states nor rules out. If he is right, the ancient story would be a memory of visitors arriving by aircraft.

discussion.by: The Book of Enoch (translated by R. H. Charles)
discussion.text: The book says the two hundred "descended" on "the summit of Mount Hermon" (6:6), and has God tell the Watchers that they were "spiritual, living the eternal life, and immortal", and that "as for the spiritual ones of the heaven, in heaven is their dwelling" (15:6 to 7). The book tells spirits come down from heaven; the step from that descent to beings at the helms of aerospace vehicles is the teller's reading, which he gives as his belief, and the text neither states nor excludes it.
